newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA STRIKE HALTS CAPE TOWN'S BUILDING INDUSTRY.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA STRIKE HALTS CAPE TOWN'S BUILDING INDUSTRY.

text.p: An average of about 25 percent of Cape Town workers responded to the call by the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) for a 24-hour strike on Monday, officials said.
The Cape Chamber of Commerce and Industry said the response had been "patchy", varying from sector to sector.
The hardest hit was the building sector with absenteeism at 80 percent, followed by the clothing sector where between 60 and 70 percent of workers stayed away from work, a chamber spokesman said.
The rail service around the city had not been affected while the bus service reported a 14 percent stayaway which left the services largly immune to the strike.
The banking and retail sectors had also not been affected.

Several thousand chanting workers gathered on the Grand Parade at midday and then marched to parliament to protest against the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill which has already passed through cabinet and is expected to be tabled before parliament soon.
Cosatu is demanding a 40-hour working week, six months maternity leave and double pay for Sunday work.
